newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine energy board says to hike fuel prices.
newsitem.headline: Philippine energy board says to hike fuel prices.

text.p: The government's Energy Regulatory Board (ERB) said on Tuesday it will raise most fuel prices this week as a result of higher Singapore posted prices.
"Countries have started to store fuel for the winter season creating pressure on Singapore posted prices of fuel used for heating," ERB Chair Bayani Faylona told Reuters.
Faylona said that based on initial computation by the ERB, price of diesel oil will increase by 46 centavos per liter, followed by aviation turbo by 40 centavos and fuel oil by 35 centavos.
Kerosene will be raised by 34 centavos per liter, liquefied petroleum gasoline by 8 centavos and regular gasoline by 3 centavos.

Only the price of unleaded premium gasoline may be reduced by 1 centavo while price of premium gasoline may remain unchanged. Faylona said the oil price adjustments will likely be announced on October 16 to 17.
This is the third time government will adjust petroleum prices using a monthly automatic oil adjustment formula based on Singapore posted prices as an interim step to full oil industry deregulation.
